headline: Public Law 116-217 authorizes a monument in Washington, D.C., honoring the women's suffrage movement and the 19th Amendment, paid for only by private donations.
what_it_does: The law allows a monument called the Every Word We Utter Monument to be built on federal land in the District of Columbia. It commemorates the women's suffrage movement and the passage of the 19th Amendment, which gave women the right to vote. No federal money may be used for the monument's establishment expenses. The Every Word We Utter Monument organization must collect contributions and pay all costs itself.
when_it_takes_effect: Upon enactment on December 17, 2020. The summary gives no other dates.
